text:
julie_cust: Hey team — after upgrading to Private v2 our customers are seeing SSE streams drop after a few minutes. They get a partial last event, client reconnects, and sometimes the app reports duplicate tokens billed. We have an on-prem ingress + corporate proxy chain.
support_alex: Sorry you're hitting this, can you paste a short timeline + any headers you saw? is this consistent across users or a single customer?
julie_cust: Hitting 4 different users behind the same corp proxy (Zscaler + in-house HAProxy). Timeline: connect -> stream fine for ~90-180s -> chunk stops mid-event -> client reconnect -> new stream ok. Billing shows two partial responses counted.
eng_maya: Thanks. Two likely causes: mid-path TLS interception/proxy closing idle tunneled connections, or MTU/fragmentation leading to proxy injecting RST/FIN on large chunk boundaries. Also token rotation on reconnect could cause brief 401s which client retries and server counts as new usage.
infra_ben: Can you capture a tcpdump on the ingress box showing the last few packets when a disconnect happens? Also capture the raw SSE bytes so we can see if the stream ended with a complete event or was truncated.
julie_cust: Attaching a short excerpt (sanitized):
```
GET /v1/streams/chat HTTP/1.1
Host: inference.private.company.local
Accept: text/event-stream
Authorization: Bearer redacted
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

<...stream data...>
000000a: {"delta":"Hello, wor"}
[connection reset by peer]
```
support_alex: That reset by peer lines up with a proxy closing the connection mid-chunk. Can you check HAProxy and Zscaler logs for any TLS-inspect or max-header/body limits at the same time?
network_ryan: If corporate TLS inspection is modifying TLS, it sometimes turns the backend connection into http close semantics. Also some proxies will buffer chunked responses and if they hit their buffer limit they close the client socket. On HAProxy, check for 'maxconn' and 'tune.bufsize' / 'timeout tunnel' settings.
julie_cust: We're seeing frequent lines in HAProxy logs: 'TRUNC resp body'.
eng_maya: OK that's helpful. Two actionable repro steps for you to run (fast):
1) Reproduce with a direct curl to the private ingress bypassing corp proxy:
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://inference.private.company.local/v1/streams/chat" > sse_dump_direct.txt
```
2) Reproduce through corp proxy (same client) and capture tcpdump on ingress + proxy:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w sse_repro.pcap host inference.private.company.local and port 443
```
Compare whether the last packet is a FIN/RST from the proxy or the server.
support_alex: Also look for duplicate billing traces tied to two distinct requests from the same session id — that often means the client retried with a rotated token or the reconnect created a new session before the server marked the previous session closed. Can you confirm your client uses the same conversation/session identifier on reconnect?
julie_cust: Client keeps the same conversation id but we refresh tokens periodically using the refresh endpoint and the reconnect occurs right after token rotation.
eng_maya: That matches a race: reconnect happens during token swap -> new connection authenticated -> server treats as new stream -> billing increments. Two ways to fix: ensure token rotation happens off-stream (do not refresh mid-stream), or implement idempotency key / session pinning header so server attributes reconnects to same session. We're going to add server-side heuristics in the Dedicated control plane to collapse short overlap windows.
infra_ben: For the proxy truncation, quick HAProxy recommendations as a temporary mitigation: set 'tune.bufsize' larger (e.g., 32768), enable 'option http-server-close' or 'timeout tunnel 1m', and ensure 'maxhdr' isn't being hit. For TLS-inspecting appliances (Zscaler/Bluecoat) ask security to add a bypass rule for your ingress host for streaming endpoints.
network_ryan: Also check path MTU issues if you're seeing fragmentation: enable MSS clamping on edge routers (set TCP MSS to 1400) or adjust kernel iptables to avoid DF-bit problems. If PMTU blackhole exists, large chunks crossing a device can get dropped causing mid-chunk truncation.
julie_cust: We tried bypassing Zscaler and get a steady stream for 30+ minutes with no resets. With Zscaler in path stream cuts after ~2 minutes.
support_alex: That confirms corpproxy is the interceptor. Short-term workaround: use smaller chunk sizes on the server side to avoid large TCP segments and add client reconnect de-dup logic. For Private/Dedicated tenants we can toggle a per-tenant 'sse_chunk_bytes' to 512 to test.
eng_maya: For a definitive reproduce, please run these and drop the two pcaps and the sse_dump outputs into the support ticket. We'll triage with the network ops team and open an action with Zscaler if needed.
julie_cust: Will do. One more oddity — sometimes the client reports a parse error because event boundaries split in the middle of a multi-byte UTF-8 sequence. Could that be from chunk cut mid-character?
eng_maya: Yes. If a chunk cut occurs mid-character, the SSE client may fail to decode and close the stream. Workaround: server-side ensure chunks align with codepoint boundaries; we can also advise your client to use a tolerant UTF-8 decoder that buffers incomplete sequences across chunks.
deploy-bot: [deploy] Rolling back temporary change to chunking on dedicated-node-12 completed by infra_ben
support_alex: Thanks everyone — next steps for customer: capture the two tcpdumps (bypass vs corp path), collect HAProxy "TRUNC resp body" log lines with timestamps, and try server-side reduced chunk size. We'll follow up after you upload artifacts.
julie_cust: Uploading pcaps now, thanks all :thumbsup:
